title: M3-CAD designs antimicrobial QLX-3DV peptides
summary: M3-CAD combines sequence, predicted structural and physicochemical features in a multimodal peptide-design pipeline. The journal study reports in-vitro activity for selected QLX-3DV peptides, including untemplated candidates, against tested bacterial strains; selected leads also received additional host-toxicity and mouse wound-infection assays. These are selected preclinical results, not evidence of clinical efficacy or safety. The article cites an earlier M3-CAD/QL-AMP-1 preprint; this entry is restricted to the reported QLX-3DV study result and does not claim the pipeline itself as new.
organization: Qilu Hospital of Shandong University; Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

evidence.tested: Selected designed peptides were synthesized and tested in vitro; selected leads were also examined in mouse wound infection and host-toxicity assays.
evidence.unknown: Clinical efficacy and safety, independent replication and full sequence-level comparison with the earlier M3-CAD preprint are not established here.
evidence.ai_role: M3-CAD uses multimodal learned sequence and predicted-structure representations with activity-related objectives to generate and rank peptides for experimental testing.

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text including publication metadata, methods and experimental results.
